note: Colouring 1 puts a short grey line at the red stripe's lower edge, echoing the original's pale edge highlight, while colouring 2 only extends the red staircase; the difference is a few pixels.

Colouring 1 renders several flame and hat cells in dull olive/red patches, while colouring 2 uses bright red/yellow orange that matches the fire and its neighbours.

Colouring 2 draws the bright cream line under the car consistently in white and adds blue dots to the dark blue body, while colouring 1 makes parts of the line and texture dim grey, so the line alternates grey and white.

Colouring 1 keeps the letter-top serifs and the B's counter edges bright yellow like the gold letters, while colouring 2 makes them dim olive bars that read greenish and cell-aligned against the bright letter bodies.
Colouring 1 scatters grey, green and bright red specks over the warm brown torch, hat and face, while colouring 2 keeps these cells olive/yellow on black in the picture's warm palette.

Colouring 1 puts a stray bright-white hook at the dark edge of the sunset, while colouring 2 continues the dark-red staircase of the edge smoothly.

Colouring 2 fills the 2x2 cells with a flat dark-red square that stands out as a block among dithered reds, while colouring 1 keeps a red/black dither continuous with the cells above, though darker and noisier than the smooth original.

Colouring 2 puts green dots into the olive-brown hair, yellow where the original is reddish brown and white on brown; colouring 1 uses yellow and red there, which fit better, though colouring 2's red for one hair cell is slightly better.
Colouring 1 fills two cells with flat dark red, which show as squares in the dithered bright red and black; colouring 2 continues the dither smoothly.

Colouring 1 turns four cells of the golden-yellow area into flat olive (dark yellow) patches that stand out as blocks; colouring 2 keeps bright yellow with black dots, which blends with the neighbouring cells.
Colouring 2 renders five flame cells in dark red and dark yellow, which show as dull khaki squares next to bright red and yellow cells; colouring 1 keeps the flame bright and continuous.
Both use the same colour pairs in every cell, so they differ only in dithering noise.

Colouring 1 renders the pink sky and lavender clouds with dark magenta on black and a grey-pink magenta and white checker, giving dark blotchy cells; colouring 2 uses bright magenta with blue, so the sky stays smooth and the clouds read as bluish.
The outlined cells on the leaf-covered path use the same ink/paper pairs (red/yellow, red/white, black/yellow) in both, differing only in dither noise.
The outlined dragon-head cells (green/blue, black/green) have the same colours and proportions in both colourings; only the dither pattern differs.
